studies.title: Join algorithm × parallelism
insights: Fastest is not greenest: Sort-merge join · 8 threads finishes first, but Hash join · 1 thread uses 27% less energy while taking 30% longer.

studies.title: Storage format × compression
insights: Reading the inputs takes 92% of the energy with JSON lines + Zstd but only 29% with Parquet (uncompressed): the format changes the cost of loading, not of computing.
Parquet (uncompressed) (fastest) and Parquet + Snappy (most frugal) are statistically tied: the difference between them is within measurement noise.

studies.title: Full scan vs inverted index
insights: Inverted index repays its build energy after about 3 queries: building costs 1.79 J more than the scan's setup, then each query saves 555.53 mJ (per-query costs measured at 100 queries).
Full scan (regex) · 1 query is both the fastest and the most frugal exact option at 1 query.

studies.title: Batch vs incremental, exact vs approximate
insights: Incremental + HyperLogLog uses 2.7× the energy of the exact Incremental panes, while erring by 1.9% on distinct users: approximate is not automatically greener.
10 % user sample uses no less energy than the best exact option, Incremental panes, while erring by 15.5% on value sum: here approximation buys accuracy loss, not savings.

studies.title: No index vs B+-tree vs hash index
insights: B+-tree repays its build energy after about 149 queries: building costs 0.41 J more than the scan's setup, then each query saves 2.77 mJ (per-query costs measured at 1,000 and 100,000 queries).
Hash index repays its build energy after about 213 queries: building costs 0.57 J more than the scan's setup, then each query saves 2.70 mJ (per-query costs measured at 1,000 and 100,000 queries).
